Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

llmsa (development version)

  • Ordinal and binary fits reject confounded random-effect variances before calling the engine, including interactions and terms spanned by fixed effects. The check includes the fixed latent residual variance and frequency weights: zero-weight rows contribute no information, and a random term with one observation per level cannot be separated from the residual. Errors name only the affected terms and explain residual confounding when present. Sparse cross-products preserve this check for designs with thousands of factor levels without dense projection blocks. Integer weights count as frequencies; if any retained weight is noninteger, each positive-weight row counts once in the check. Engine weights are unchanged. The help page documents the limitations of term selection with zero-weight rows. Identifiable designs retain their existing engine fits; ordinal singularity concerns random effects only.

  • Latent fits apply subset, weights, offset and na.action before selecting model terms, so data and study counts describe the analysed rows. Ordinal offsets are kept in data$.msa_offset; with frequency weights, n$observations counts rows and nobs(model) reports the weight sum. Stored engine calls retain evaluated arguments and can be evaluated again outside the original caller, including for binary refits and bootstraps.

  • Explicit ordinal and binary levels must contain distinct, non-missing, non-empty labels. They determine the coding independently of the response storage type and take precedence over an ordered factor’s levels.

  • Ordinal and binary fits validate exact binary codes, explicit event labels, missing grouping values and constant categories. Dropped responses are counted in warnings and in the returned study size.

  • msa_fit() now reports final-engine converged independently of singular. The actual clmm optimizer determines success, including its matrix fallback; stored ordinal and binary failure diagnoses produce warnings. Numeric fits retain their existing final-engine warning behavior.

  • Two-level ordinal components always warn about the positive bias of the range method, beta-hat^2 / 2, which does not subtract the AIAG correction EV^2 / (n * r). Both print methods identify every derived component; msa_grr() retains the component names in derived. The two_level study and the validation vignette document the method and its limitations.

  • The validation vignette adds live ordinal and binary comparisons, separates latent ICC from rptR’s default scale convention, and reads reproducible recovery-study results with MCSE. Offline anchor copies carry SHA-256 provenance. Three simulation scripts retain fit failures and seeds, support separate scenario runs, and ship short reproducibility runs; full simulation findings require the operator’s later runs.

  • Default numeric msa_fit() preserves numeric input precision and completes REML using balanced-design formulas or an analytic constrained solution. The returned lme4 model stays on the original scale; numerics reports the method and diagnostics. Explicit fitting arguments retain the direct lme4 path, and bootstrap refits use ordinary lme4 optimization.

  • Numeric fits diagnose constant or non-finite responses, missing grouping values, degenerate residual variance and original-scale precision loss. The default path checks the residual model space before starting lme4, including unbalanced multi-factor studies with missing responses or cells. Failed initialization now gives a named error with the engine’s cause and preserves start warnings, including for small positive residual variance. Arithmetic warnings and errors while constructing the original-scale model become named precision errors; final convergence warnings remain active. Numeric NaN and the string "NaN" are treated as missing responses. Explicit subset, weights and offset expressions use the fitting data; counts and row mappings describe the observations actually analysed. Stored fitting controls remain usable outside the original caller’s scope. A failed fit stops msa_plan() with its diagnostic.

  • msa_grr() applies the minimum ndc convention and reports undefined ratios as NA when total variance is zero, with verdict undetermined. Custom thresholds must be finite, numeric, nonnegative and nondecreasing.

  • The numeric validation vignette computes literature, NIST and package-oracle comparisons offline. Public builds include verified free NIST inputs and complete anchor copies; protected AIAG data remain local and their public comparison is marked as not rerun.

  • backend_openai_compatible() now omits temperature from the request when temperature = NULL. It supports a per-row system message and records response IDs, model snapshots, usage, fingerprints and requested/reported provider routing.

  • backend_openai_compatible() records a non-empty message.reasoning of the reply as meta$reasoning (Qwen3-32B via OpenRouter returns its reasoning there). reasoning_details is not stored, and only message.content is parsed.

  • backend_openai_compatible() records finish_reason and native_finish_reason of the first choice as meta$finish_reason and meta$native_finish_reason when they are non-empty strings, and the request timeout as meta$timeout_s. The default timeout = 120 is unchanged.

  • parse_choice(whole_word = TRUE) matches whole phrases, preferring longer phrases and rejecting ambiguous classifications. The default remains unchanged.

  • msa_run(parse_by_prompt = ...) can select a parser for each prompt while retaining the raw response and the existing resumable store format. Numeric JSON metadata are now stored without rounding; small recorded API costs previously could be rounded to zero.

  • msa_report(assessment = ...) accepts validated application criteria, an overall decision and additional report sections, including a robustness half-normal plot.

  • The internal AP1 pipeline adds frozen study inputs, a YAML plan, an explicit mock/API runner, pilot checks and per-model assessment. Its functions are not exported. AP1 results are provisional until the M1 statistical validation.

  • The AP1 plan requires a client timeout per model (timeout_s, 1800 s for all three models), which the runner passes to backend_openai_compatible(). The AP1 pilot has a fifth pass rule, backend_errors: a backend error share of at most error_share_trigger per model, unreadable answers not counted. The pilot summary reports the maximum latency.

  • The internal AP1 runner repeats a call that failed before its request was sent (name resolution, connection, TLS handshake, or a timeout in these phases) after pauses of 30 s, doubling up to 600 s and at most 12 h per call (plan field network), instead of storing it as a backend error; then it stops without a row for that call. Such calls record network_retries and network_wait_s. The runner logs its progress with timestamps to stderr.

llmsa 0.1.0

First public release.

  • Crossed study design (msa_design()), execution with an audit trail and resumable store (msa_run()), import of external results (as_msa_runs()).
  • Backends: backend_mock(), backend_ellmer(), backend_openai_compatible(); parsers for numbers, labels and JSON fields.
  • Variance components for numeric, ordinal and binary outcomes (msa_fit()), gauge R&R statistics with AIAG classification (msa_grr()), parametric bootstrap intervals (msa_boot()).
  • Attribute agreement with Krippendorff’s alpha and Cohen’s kappa (msa_agreement()), bias and linearity (msa_bias()).
  • Plackett-Burman robustness screening with Lenth’s method (pb_design(), msa_robustness()).
  • Simulation-based study planning (msa_simulate(), msa_plan()).
  • Westgard-rule control charts for system suitability (msa_control_chart()).
  • Validation report template (msa_report()).
  • Simulated demonstration data acmg_demo and ic50_demo.

Known limitations: no bootstrap for ordinal fits; batched multi-item prompts (position and carry-over effects) and free-text outcomes judged by a second model are planned for a later release.
